entries.claim: When put-down FK opens while the container is still visibly elevated, review before the opening command: an after-measured aperture guard can return only after the container has already fallen. In this episode a 40-control authorization returned after16; clear airborne separation was visible by offset13, and the container then landed near its original position. No recovery or task failure occurred, but the guard did not prevent the drop.
entries.conditions: VideoUnmaskSwap put-down following a completed lift, specifically when current RGB and candidate FK suggest opening before table support. Keep ordinary approach duration advice separate. The observation does not establish a universally safe prefix or prove that dropping will always cause failure. Compare with the existing placement-separation observation and ordinary40-control duration prior; this entry adds conditional release-risk scheduling only.

entries.claim: A first container's cube becoming visible may be too weak a milestone for switching immediately to put-down when the fresh pickup candidate still proposes further upward motion. Consider continuing and reviewing the ongoing lift rather than truncating it solely on color reveal. In the observed failure both requested colors were visibly revealed in order, but the first lift was replaced with put-down while further ascent was pending; premature phase transition is a hypothesis, not a proven failure cause.
entries.conditions: VideoUnmaskSwap first pickup in a multi-container sequence, without intermediate official confirmation and with only modest visible clearance while pickup FK still proposes ascent. Distinct from elevated-opening risk: the later release was at table height. Do not infer hidden registration rules, a universal height/duration threshold, or a safe budget. Ordinary approach duration advice remains unchanged; the concern is the phase-change criterion at a wake.
